guarantees.claim: On reset (rst_ni low), rx_valid_q is cleared to 0 on the next clock edge; when reset is inactive, rx_valid_q is driven to (tick_baud_q && bit_cnt_q == 4'h1) on each clock edge.

uncertain_points.claim: It is unclear whether the condition (bit_cnt_q == 4'h1) is the exact moment of a completed byte reception. Using a hardcoded '1' may be fragile if the bit-order or count encoding changes.
uncertain_points.cond: When baud tick occurs and bit_cnt_q reaches 1
uncertain_points.risk: rx_valid_q could be asserted at an incorrect time, causing a false data-valid strobe to downstream logic.

formal_sketch.antecedent: When baud tick occurs and bit_cnt_q reaches 1
formal_sketch.consequent: It is unclear whether the condition (bit_cnt_q == 4'h1) is the exact moment of a completed byte reception. Using a hardcoded '1' may be fragile if the bit-order or count encoding changes

security_implications: If rx_valid_q is incorrectly asserted due to a glitch or mismatched bit-count condition, a downstream FIFO may capture invalid data, violating communication integrity. This does not expose secrets but can cause data corruption.
